Loading libraries
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(flexdashboard)
library(p8105.datasets)
  data("instacart")
```

Loading data
```{r}
instacart_df = 
  instacart |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  group_by(
    product_id, product_name, department
  ) |> 
  summarize(
    n_purchases = n(),
    mean_cart_position = mean(add_to_cart_order),
    reorder_rate = mean(reordered)
  ) |> 
  ungroup()

instacart |> 
  count(department) |> 
  arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  print(n=21)
```

### Scatterplot: 
* no missing variables through skimr on instacart
* used view(instacart_df) to evaluate that mean_cart position follows a right skewed histogram distribution
* skimr on instacart_df showed that p75 for n_purchases was 18 and p100 was 18726 so decided to use 20 as cutoff point
* After finding `r n_distinct(pull(instacart, department))` departments, I used print(n=21) to list the total number of categories; i removed "missing" category in my department filter
* scatter plot shows that if the product was placed earlier in the cart, it tended to be reordered more. Earlier cart position and more reordering seemed to be more common 
```{r}
instacart_df |> 
  filter(department %in% c("dairy eggs", "produce", "canned goods", "beverages", "deli", "snacks", "pantry", "frozen", "meat seafood", "household", "bakery", "personal care", "dry goods pasta", "babies", "other", "breakfast", "international", "alcohol", "bulk", "pets")) |> 
  filter(n_purchases >=19) |> 
  mutate(text_label = str_c("Product: ", product_name, "\nPurchases: ", n_purchases)) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~mean_cart_position,
    y = ~reorder_rate,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    color = ~department,
    colors = "viridis",
    text = ~text_label,
    alpha = 0.5
  )
```
